test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.text: The United Nations (UN) has six language official languages.
The term of a judge in the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is five years.
The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has five permanent members.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has fifteen judges.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The term of a judge in the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is five years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term of a judge in the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is not five years but nine years.
 
• The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.
 
• Judges of the ICJ are elected by the United Nations General Assembly and the Security Council.
 
• The ICJ consists of 15 judges, who are elected to nine-year terms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The United Nations has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish.
 
• The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has five permanent members: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
 
• The ICJ's role is to settle legal disputes submitted by states and to provide advisory opinions on legal questions referred to it by authorized international organs and agencies.
